title: JavaScript Prototypes Core Check
description: Check your understanding of the prototype chain, own vs inherited properties, Object.create, __proto__, constructor prototypes, and classes.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is the prototype chain used for?

options.text: Looking up properties and methods through linked objects

questions.explanation: When a property is not found directly on an object, JavaScript searches the object's prototype chain.

options.text: A property that exists directly on an object
A property that can never be changed
A property only classes can create

questions.explanation: An own property is stored directly on the object, not inherited through the prototype chain.

questions.prompt: Which method is recommended for checking only own properties?
questions.explanation: `Object.hasOwn()` checks direct properties only, while `in` checks own and inherited properties.

options.text: Creates a new object whose prototype is `parent`

questions.explanation: `Object.create(parent)` creates a new object linked to `parent` through the prototype chain.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred modern way to inspect an object's prototype?
questions.explanation: `Object.getPrototypeOf()` is the standard modern API for reading an object's prototype.

options.text: A commonly seen accessor for an object's prototype
The same thing as a function's `prototype` property

questions.explanation: `__proto__` points to an object's prototype, but modern code should usually prefer `Object.getPrototypeOf()`.

questions.prompt: What does a constructor function's `.prototype` property provide?

options.text: The object that instances created with `new` inherit from
A JSON representation of the function

questions.explanation: When `new Constructor()` runs, the new object is linked to `Constructor.prototype`.

questions.prompt: Where should shared methods usually be placed when using constructor functions?

options.text: Inside every instance as a new function

questions.explanation: Putting shared methods on `.prototype` lets instances share one method instead of creating a copy per instance.

questions.prompt: Where do normal class methods usually live?

options.text: Directly as own properties on every instance

questions.explanation: Class methods are prototype methods, so instances inherit them from `ClassName.prototype`.
`key in object` returns true for both own and inherited properties.

questions.prompt: Why should you generally avoid modifying built-in prototypes like `Array.prototype`?

options.text: It can cause conflicts, surprising behavior, and maintenance problems
It makes arrays stop working immediately
It prevents objects from having own properties

questions.explanation: Modifying built-in prototypes affects shared global behavior and can conflict with libraries or future JavaScript features.

options.text: Accidentally or maliciously changing shared prototypes such as `Object.prototype`

questions.explanation: Prototype pollution changes shared prototypes and can cause unexpected inherited properties or security problems.
